execution.progress: Paid work in twelve one-round increments per bay whose exact job, reserved pieces per bay and increment, installed parts and site persist across interruption; resume pays only the next increment after revalidation; completion, cancellation, failure and death settle once. Inspect, repair and dismantle are single rounds.

details.costs: Study: 4 rounds. Start: x, y (the centre of the whole footprint), orientation (degrees; 0 points every low roof edge toward increasing x, where wind comes from, and the shared open side toward decreasing x), bays (2-4, default 2) and materials as exact owned, untreated whole units totalling 13 branch, 4 vine and 6 bark per bay (26, 8 and 12 for two bays); stone is not accepted. The footprint is 2 m across by 2 m per bay along the ridge, of ordinary dry soil, inside the world, unobstructed and unoccupied, and you stand within reach of the first bay; a 1 m strip along the open side must be walkable, inside the world and free of solid objects. Twelve paid increments per bay, one round and 1 energy each (24 rounds and 24 energy for two bays), bay after bay: 2 posts, 3 ridge and braces, 3 ribs and binding, 3 roofing courses, 1 final check; start pays the first and the same action continues each round; each increment needs reach to the bay being built. Resume pays the next increment of the unfinished work; cancel takes one round and no energy. Inspect: a bay in reach as target, one round, 0.2 energy, covering every bay of the structure in reach. Repair (builder only): target bay, increment 1-11 and the exact replacement units of that increment, one round, 1 energy. Dismantle (builder only): target bay, one round and 1 energy per stage, removing that bay's last installed stage. Gathering, travel, messages and probe tests are separate actions with their own costs.
details.effects: Reserved materials stay carried and owned until each paid increment moves them into its bay as installed parts with the same quantity, origin and age; nothing is created or used up. Each bay is a full braced lean-to with its own posts and braces (no spanning roof or shared members) and its own 2 m x 1 m covered floor under a 1.2 m ridge. A bay's final stability, binding, roof-load, runoff and open-approach checks commission that bay alone. While exactly one person lies wholly on a commissioned bay's floor in rain and wind up to 0.8, that bay removes up to 50% of the rain part and up to 35% of the wind part of the existing outdoor exposure chill, scaled by its roof condition, by the share of the body under its roof along the wind-driven rain, and for wind by how directly its low edge faces the wind; people on other bays do not change it, but two people on the same bay floor, wind into the open side, stronger weather or water pooling on the floor give that bay no protection. Air temperature, hunger, nutrition and rest are unchanged, and shelters never stack. Each round every installed part wears by 0.0005 + 0.002 x rain + 0.002 x wind; a part below condition 0.5 makes that bay unsafe with no protection until repair and a passing reinspection. Changes in who lies on each bay floor are reported. Repair restores only the replaced parts; removed and dismantled parts return to the ground at the bay with their condition and can be reused. Work not continued in a round pauses; a lost reserved material stops it. Cancel returns uninstalled materials once, leaves partly built bays unfinished and keeps commissioned bays; death stops the work, drops uninstalled materials where the person died and leaves installed parts. Nobody else is moved, helped or given access; each person acts and pays for themselves. No reward, mastery or refund.

Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 4000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form.
